original_question: Does there exist an irreducible component of Hilb_d(A^3) whose dimension is smaller than the expected value 3d, and does there exist an irreducible component of the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3, 0) whose dimension is smaller than 2(d-1)?
target_in_paper: Problem IV in §2.1 ("Irreducible components") of arXiv:2307.08777: the existence of low-dimensional irreducible components of Hilb_d(A^3) and of the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3,0).
correct_elements: Your draft already lands on the exact target in the paper: Problem IV. It names the correct two moduli spaces, uses the correct threshold dimensions 3d and 2(d-1), and asks for strict inequality in dimension, which is exactly the paper's formulation.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k, so the ambient space should be written as A^3_k rather than an unspecified A^3 (§1.3, pp. 2-3).
The existential quantifier over the degree is implicit in the paper: the question is whether there exists some positive integer d with such a component (Problem IV, p. 5).

Hilb_d(A^3,0) should be defined stand-alone as the punctual Hilbert scheme at the origin, i.e. the fiber over d[0] of the Hilbert-Chow map, equivalently the scheme of degree-d subschemes supported at 0 (§1.3, pp. 2-3).

The phrase "expected value" is not the paper's wording. In context, 3d is the dimension of the smoothable component of Hilb_d(A^3), and 2(d-1) is the dimension of the curvilinear component of Hilb_d(A^3,0) (§2.1, p. 4).
It should be explicit that "component" means an irreducible component of the scheme.
The two existence questions are separate in the paper; it does not require the same d to work for both (Problem IV, p. 5).

A characteristic-zero hypothesis should not be added to the question itself: the paper formulates Problem IV over the general algebraically closed base field k, even though nearby known reducibility bounds are summarized in characteristic zero (§2.1, p. 5).
refined_question: Over an algebraically closed field k, does there exist a positive integer d such that the Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3_k) has an irreducible component of dimension strictly smaller than 3d? Likewise, does there exist a positive integer d such that the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^3_k,0), namely the scheme of degree-d subschemes of A^3_k supported at the origin, has an irreducible component of dimension strictly smaller than 2(d-1)?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper's exact statement: it matches Problem IV in §2.1 on p. 5. To make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the notation from §1.3: k is algebraically closed, Hilb_d(X) denotes the Hilbert scheme of d points, and Hilb_d(X,x) is the fiber of the Hilbert-Chow map over d[x], equivalently the locus of degree-d subschemes supported at x (pp. 2-3). The numbers 3d and 2(d-1) are not presented in the paper as generic "expected dimensions"; they come from the dimensions of the smoothable component of Hilb_d(X) and the curvilinear component of Hilb_d(X,x) for smooth X, specialized to X = A^3_k in §2.1 (p. 4). The sentence immediately after Problem IV adds the nearby paper-specific context: low-dimensional components of Hilb_d(A^3_k,0) matter for studying Hilb_d(A^3_k), and the paper explicitly says it is unknown whether a small punctual component forces a small component of Hilb_d(A^3_k) (p. 5).
